column3: “had relations with” renders “knew,” and “a manchild with the help of the LORD” renders “a man with the LORD.”
“in the course of time” renders “at the end of days.”
“will not your countenance be lifted up” supplies “your countenance” for the single word “lifting up,” whose meaning is uncertain.
“told” renders “said to,” but no words follow in the Hebrew; the Samaritan Pentateuch and the Greek add “Let us go out to the field.”
“its strength” renders “its strength (koach),” the soil's yield, and “a vagrant and a wanderer” renders “a wanderer and a fugitive” (also in verse 14).
“My punishment” renders “my iniquity,” a word that can mean both guilt and its punishment.
“Therefore” follows the Hebrew; the Greek and other versions read “Not so.”
“the forger of all implements” renders “a sharpener of every worker (tool).”
“men began” renders an impersonal “it was begun.”
